dividends.title: Dividend patterns
dividends.intro: Historical price behaviour around cash dividends, calculated from stored market data. Patterns describe the past and do not predict the next dividend.

dividends.sourceNote: Past ex-dates and amounts come from stored Yahoo chart events. Future dates below are estimates, not KSEI confirmations.
dividends.patternRule: Filters require at least two priced dividends and an average traded value of {value} per session over 20 sessions.
dividends.insufficient: The dividend sample or trading-value coverage is insufficient for these filters.
dividends.noPattern: None of the documented filters match this stock's observed history.
dividends.projectionRule: Same weekday 52 weeks after a payment in the past year; removed if a newer dated dividend is within 60 days of the estimate.
dividends.noProjection: No anniversary projection is available from the stored dividend history.
dividends.historyNote: Prices are split-adjusted daily closes. Run-up compares cum-date close with 15 sessions earlier; recovery counts the ex-date as session one.
dividends.noHistory: No cash dividends with usable prices are stored for this period.

meta.title: HAKA PRO — IDX stock research
meta.description: HAKA PRO is a research workspace for Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) stocks: prices, foreign and broker flow, financial statements, insider disclosures and structured analysis, with every number dated.

hero.eyebrow: Research for Indonesia Stock Exchange stocks
hero.title: IDX stock research, with every number dated.
hero.subtitle: HAKA PRO puts prices, foreign and broker flow, financial statements, insider disclosures and structured analysis for every listed company into one calm workspace, and tells you how fresh each figure is.
hero.noteSignedOut: Market data is for signed-in users. Research only: HAKA PRO never tells you what to buy.
hero.noteSignedIn: Research only: HAKA PRO never tells you what to buy.

features.title: Everything you check before a decision, in one place
features.intro: No more jumping between broker apps, exchange PDFs and spreadsheets.

flow.title: Follow the money
flow.body: Daily foreign net buying and selling, broker summaries for any session or date range, top buyers against top sellers with their average prices, and who has been accumulating.

financials.title: Read the fundamentals
financials.body: Income statements, balance sheets and cash flows, quarterly or annual, by year, with a warning when a company's latest report is overdue.

insiders.title: See who traded
insiders.body: Director, commissioner and major-holder disclosures grouped by holder. Custodian accounts are flagged so they aren't mistaken for owners.

analysis.title: Understand the technicals
analysis.body: A score with its contributing factors, moving averages, RSI, MACD, pivot levels, and how similar situations played out in the stock's own history, in plain language.

history.title: Charts and history
history.body: Candles with indicators, a daily price table you can filter by date, monthly seasonality and the trade-by-trade tape for any session.

discover.title: Find ideas
discover.body: Strategy matches that explain why a stock appeared, a screener, market movers, the largest companies by market cap and recent ownership changes.

freshness.title: Every number tells you how old it is
freshness.intro: A price from last Friday shouldn't look like a price from this minute. HAKA PRO labels every dataset with its state and as-of date, and never calls data live when it isn't.

states.DELAYED: Today's session while trading is running, a little behind the exchange.
states.HISTORICAL: A past period or a longer date range.
states.STALE: Older than data that should already be out, such as an overdue financial report.
states.UNAVAILABLE: The date can't be confirmed, so we say so instead of guessing.

freshness.hover: Hover or tap any badge in the app to see the exact date, period and source.

how.title: From ticker to understanding in three steps

steps.title: Search
steps.body: Press Ctrl K (⌘K on Mac) and type a ticker or company name.

steps.title: Get the overview
steps.body: Key metrics, valuation and short observations on price, flow, ownership and financials.

steps.title: Go deeper, then keep watch
steps.body: Open the Flow, Analysis, Financials, Insiders or History tabs, then add the stock to your watchlist and set alerts.

observed.title: Observed, not predicted
observed.body: We describe what happened in the data. Analysis outlooks are labelled as calculations, never as our advice.

neutral.title: Neutral language
neutral.body: No rockets, no must-buys. Brokers are trading firms, not owners, and the app says so.

privacy.title: Your account, your lists
privacy.body: Watchlists and alerts belong to your account. Identity numbers found in public filings are removed before anything is shown.

local.title: Made for Indonesia
local.body: Bahasa Indonesia first, English when you need it, rupiah formatting and the IDX trading calendar built in.

items.a: No. During a trading session prices are delayed, and after the close you see end-of-day data. Every figure shows its as-of date, and the time of the last trade when there is one.
No. HAKA PRO is for research and education. Where an analysis includes an outlook or price levels, it is shown as a calculation from the data, not a recommendation. Decisions are yours.
Companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, more than 900 of them. Daily history starts in January 2020 for most; newer listings start from their listing date.
Yes, to see market data. Your account also keeps your watchlist and alerts.

items.q: Does it work on my phone?
items.a: Yes. HAKA PRO works on phones, tablets and desktops, in a light or dark theme.

items.q: Where does the data come from?
items.a: From Indonesian market data sources covering prices, broker activity, financial reports and disclosures. Each dataset shows its date so you can judge it yourself.

final.title: Start your next IDX research session with the facts.
final.body: Open any listed company and see its prices, flows, fundamentals and disclosures side by side.

footer.tagline: Indonesian equity research by Heulau Lab.
footer.disclaimer: For research and education only, not investment advice. Past results don't predict future ones.

ownershipUpload.title: Upload the ≥1% shareholder list
ownershipUpload.intro: KSEI's monthly ≥1% shareholder list is published only as an announcement on the IDX website, which blocks the engine. Download the file in your browser and upload it here; the engine parses it, stores it and compares it with the previous month.
ownershipUpload.step1: Open the IDX announcements, find the latest above-1% shareholder list and download the PDF:
ownershipUpload.step2: Pick the month of the list's position (not the upload date) and, if there is one, enter the announcement number as the reference.
ownershipUpload.step3: Upload the file. What was read and the per-holder changes appear on Ownership Changes and on each stock's Ownership tab.
ownershipUpload.fileHint: PDF, CSV or XLSX, up to 20 MB. The same file is never processed twice.

groups.title: Conglomerate Groups
groups.intro: How the listed companies of major business groups moved over a session window: price change, traded value, breadth and an estimate of net foreign flow. Measured facts, not a call to buy or sell.
groups.intradayNote: intraday snapshot (delayed); foreign data arrives with the end-of-day prices
groups.howToRead: Change is weighted by each stock's traded value in the window (the simple average is shown next to it). Net foreign is an estimate: foreign buy minus sell shares × the session close, summed over the window, counted only for stocks with foreign data on every session. When price and foreign flow point opposite ways, the card says so.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.intro: How HAKA PRO reads data: where it comes from, when it arrives, what each signal means, and the limits we hold ourselves to. Every threshold on this page is read directly from the configuration the data engine uses.

principles.title: Principles
principles.observe: We show observations, not advice. Labels say what the data shows, such as "Volume 2.3× the 20-session average", not what to do about it.
principles.trace: Every figure has a data date and a source. The session date or position date is always shown next to the data.
principles.missing: Data that is absent is marked "not available yet", never treated as zero.
principles.counter: Observations pointing the other way are shown next to the signals, never hidden.

sources.title: Data sources and their delays
sources.intro: All data is end of day (EOD) unless stated otherwise. There is no real-time price feed.

arjum.name: HAKA PRO Engine (foreign flow, broker & insider data)
arjum.what: Foreign buying and selling per stock, price history, broker summaries, insider transactions for the stock pages.
arjum.when: After the close. The data engine collects foreign flow at 19:00 and 21:00 WIB on trading days, most liquid stocks first, within a daily quota. Stocks the quota does not reach have no foreign data for that session, so their foreign signals are "not available yet".

prices.name: Data engine daily prices (Yahoo Finance, TradingView, Pasardana)
prices.what: Open, high, low, close, volume and value; the list of active issuers and their sectors; the previous session's trade count.
prices.when: From about 16:35–16:45 WIB on trading days, with refetches until 20:45 WIB. Trade counts often arrive only the next session or from the HAKA PRO Engine, so the value-per-trade signal can be "not available yet".

ksei.name: ≥1% shareholder list (KSEI, uploaded by an admin)
ksei.what: ≥1% holders per issuer, investor type (for example CP for corporations), shares and percentage, compared with the month before.
ksei.when: Monthly. IDX publishes the list on its own site and a HAKA PRO admin uploads it by hand, usually days to weeks after the position date. Until a list is uploaded, the KSEI signal and view are empty.

intraday.name: Intraday snapshots
intraday.what: Running prices for the movers list and stock quotes.
intraday.when: Delayed by about 10 minutes and always labelled delayed. The radar does not use them; it only reads stored daily sessions.

radar.title: Radar signals
radar.intro: Each signal is evaluated on its own over the newest stored session. A signal "fires" when the observed value reaches its threshold. A signal whose data is incomplete is marked not available and is not counted.
radar.windowBaseline: Newest session vs the {baseline} before it

describe.foreignNetBuy5: Foreign net buying (shares bought minus shares sold) over {window} sessions, as a share of those sessions' total volume.
describe.foreignNetBuy20: The same over {window} sessions. Needs foreign data on every session in the window.
describe.volumeSpike: Newest session volume divided by the average volume of the {baseline} sessions before it.
describe.closeAboveAverage: Newest close compared with the average close of {baseline} sessions (including the newest).
describe.priceUp5: Close change from the session before the window to the newest session, over {window} sessions.
describe.orderSizeSpike: Newest value per trade (value divided by trade count) divided by its average over the {baseline} sessions before. Orders much larger than usual can show up here.
describe.kseiHolderIncrease: Number of ≥1% holders whose shares rose against the month before. Holders newly listed at ≥1% are not counted because their earlier holding is unknown.

radar.ranking: Order: stocks with the most signals first, then by the newest session's traded value. At most {limit} stocks are shown; the full count is still reported.
radar.foreignCoverage: Because foreign data is limited by a daily quota, the radar reports how many stocks each signal could be evaluated for. A signal that is not available does not mean there was no activity.

counter.title: Counter-evidence
counter.intro: Observations pointing the other way are always shown next to the signals, whatever fired. The point is that one striking figure is never read without context, for example a rising price while foreign investors are net sellers.

describe.priceVsForeign5: price direction and net foreign flow point opposite ways over the same {window} sessions (both non-zero).
describe.volumeOnDownSession: volume reached {volume} the {baseline}-session average, but that session closed lower.
describe.kseiHolderDecrease: at least {threshold} ≥1% holder reduced their shares in the newest uploaded month.

stealth.title: KSEI view: corporate holders up, price flat
stealth.intro: This view puts two data sets side by side: the change in holdings of corporate ≥1% holders, and the price change over the same period.
stealth.types: Investor types counted: {types} (the KSEI code for corporations), as stated in the list, never guessed.
stealth.combined: Corporate total = the sum of share changes of corporate holders listed in both months. Holders newly listed at ≥1% are shown separately and not summed.
stealth.price: The price counts as flat or lower when the close change between the two position dates is at most {max}. The close used is the newest session on or before each position date, at most {gap} days before it; otherwise the price is marked not available.
stealth.notIntent: This view does not infer intent, the buyer's identity or the next price move. A change in issued shares (a corporate action) is flagged because it can change holdings without any trade.

noScore.title: Why there is no score
noScore.p1: A combined score is only worth showing once each component has been tested on our own history: how often a signal was followed by a price move over the next 5 and 20 sessions, on how many samples, and with how wide an uncertainty range.
noScore.p2: That test has not been done yet. So the radar only counts the signals that fired. A signal count is not a probability and not a quality ranking; two signals are not necessarily more meaningful than one.
noScore.p3: The thresholds on this page are drafts chosen to describe unusual activity. Every change to a threshold gets a new version, and that version is shown with every result.

missing.title: Missing data
missing.body: When a signal's data is incomplete, for example foreign data outside the quota, a trade count that is not available yet, a newly listed stock, or a KSEI list that has not been uploaded, the signal is marked "not available yet". It is not counted as zero and not counted as fired.

methodology.disclaimer: This page and every view it refers to are for research and education. They describe past data; they are not investment advice, not an invitation to buy or sell, and guarantee no outcome.

stockSectorRotation.title: Stock Rotation
stockSectorRotation.intro: See which liquid issuers are strengthening or weakening against their current sector peers.
stockSectorRotation.chartDescription: Each ticker is compared with an equal-weight basket of other issuers in its current sector. The graph uses up to one year of stored sessions; choose how many recent points to show. Hover a row to highlight it.
stockSectorRotation.chartAria: Issuer relative rotation graph against a synthetic equal-weight sector peer basket.
stockSectorRotation.noPoints: There are not enough aligned price observations to calculate the graph yet.
stockSectorRotation.coverage: {count} current sector members · {eligible} liquid issuers · {shown} shown
stockSectorRotation.methodBody: The sector reference is a HakaPro synthetic, equal-weight basket built from stored split-adjusted daily closes. Each issuer is excluded from its own peer basket. A peer return needs exact closes at both endpoints. If a date has too few usable peers it is left as a gap; the next accepted observation measures from the prior accepted date without filling the missing date. This is not an official IDX sector index or proprietary JdK RRG. Current sector classifications are applied to historical prices, dividend income is excluded, and the graph describes past relative movement only. It is not a trading signal or investment advice.
stockSectorRotation.universeCapped: The engine universe is capped at 2,500 active issuers.
stockSectorRotation.liquidityRule: Only issuers with traded value on at least 15 of the latest 20 sessions are ranked.

marketReplay.intro: Replay issuer leadership alongside market breadth and sector performance on the same trading session.
marketReplay.datasetAsOf: Latest stored dates — issuer race: {race} · breadth: {breadth} · indices: {indices}
marketReplay.replayDescription: Move through stored sessions to see which stocks led while the wider market advanced or declined.
marketReplay.coverage: {priced} of {baseline} baseline names priced · {active} active names
marketReplay.universeCapped: The available issuer universe is capped; this is a partial market view.
marketReplay.missingForSession: {metric} is unavailable for this exact session.

marketReplay.noLeaders: No issuer prices are available for this session.
marketReplay.noFrames: There are no issuer race frames in this history window.
marketReplay.methodology: All figures come from the stored Engine observations. Missing dates are left missing, and issuer coverage can be partial. Price movement and breadth describe past market activity; they are not forecasts or recommendations.

sectorRotation.title: Sector Rotation
sectorRotation.intro: Relative strength and momentum of IDX-IC sectors versus a benchmark, on a four-quadrant Relative Rotation Graph. Research only — not a buy or sell signal.
sectorRotation.experimental: Experimental / internal data: sector-index values come from TradingView's public scanner and are not licensed for commercial redistribution.
sectorRotation.rrgDesc: Each sector vs {benchmark}. Centre (100, 100) is a sector trading at its own recent relative average.
sectorRotation.chartAria: Four-quadrant relative rotation graph of sectors versus the benchmark.
sectorRotation.noBenchmark: Benchmark {code} is not available in the current data.
sectorRotation.rankingsDesc: Ordered by RS-Ratio at the selected date. Hover a row to highlight it on the chart.
sectorRotation.detailEmpty: Select a sector to see its trajectory.
sectorRotation.heading: Heading
sectorRotation.insightsDesc: Deterministic notes read from the calculated points — never predictions.
sectorRotation.insufficientBody: A Relative Rotation Graph needs at least {required} aligned {interval} observations before the first point can be computed. The data currently has {available}.
sectorRotation.activation: The chart activates automatically once {required} valid observations have accumulated — no manual switch, no date threshold.
sectorRotation.historyCoverageDescription: Rows show IDX observations stored by code. RRG needs {required} dates aligned with the selected benchmark before its first point can be calculated.
sectorRotation.ingestionNote: IDX history is fetched in resumable backfill batches. Missing observations may still be waiting for collection or a successful source response.
sectorRotation.missingSectors: No IDX observations are stored yet for {count} sector(s): {sectors}. Collection progress appears in the source-history table.
sectorRotation.methodologyBody: An independent, transparent approximation (price relative → moving average → rolling z-score centred on 100). This is NOT the proprietary JdK RS-Ratio/RS-Momentum. See docs/research/sector-rotation-analysis.md.
sectorRotation.raceDescription: See which listed companies led or lagged over the same starting session. This ranks stored closes; it is not a forecast.
sectorRotation.raceCoverage: {priced} priced today · {baseline} of {active} have the shared baseline
sectorRotation.raceNoData: No issuers have closes on both the baseline and displayed sessions yet.
sectorRotation.raceMethodology: Return = close ÷ close on the first shared session − 1. Only exact daily closes are ranked; no missing prices are filled. Dividend income is excluded. Sector labels use the current security master, so historical membership may differ.

insight.momentumUp: {sector} relative momentum rose over the last three observations.
insight.momentumDown: {sector} relative momentum fell over the last three observations.
insight.crossedUp: {sector} relative strength crossed above the benchmark average (RS-Ratio ≥ 100).
insight.crossedDown: {sector} relative strength crossed below the benchmark average (RS-Ratio < 100).
